entries.name: bool_constant_int_default_oob-errored#0
entries.script: [Z1] `Coll[Boolean](true,false,true)` as a CONSTANT — the deserializer's OTHER specialised item type (`CoreDataSerializer.scala:172`, `fromArray(r.getBits(len))`) — with `.getOrElse(5, 1)`, an Int default. The specialised bridge unboxes the default to Boolean and throws `ClassCastException: class java.lang.Integer cannot be cast to class java.lang.Boolean`. **SEPARATING:** it proves B1/B2 are about SPECIALISATION and not about Byte — the same mechanism on the only other item type the wire specialises.

entries.name: bool_constant_int_default_in_range-errored#1
entries.script: [Z2] The same at index 0, IN range: still throws, because the unboxing precedes the index. **SEPARATING.**

entries.name: bool_concrete_int_default_oob-accept#2
entries.script: [Z3] The GENERIC twin — a `ConcreteCollection` of the same three booleans (`values.scala:897` calls `fromArray` at an abstract type) — `.getOrElse(5, 1)` RETURNS the mistyped default, `Int 1` at cost 79, out of a collection declared `Coll[Boolean]`. The other half of the pair: same declared type, same call, opposite outcome.

entries.name: bool_concrete_int_default_in_range-accept#3
entries.script: [Z4] The same at index 0: returns the element `true` at cost 79, where Z2 throws.

entries.name: bool_constant_bool_default_oob-accept#4
entries.script: [Z5] **CONTROL for Z1/Z2:** the specialised receiver with a WELL-TYPED default returns `false` at cost 49. It is what shows Z1/Z2 fail on the default's type and not on the receiver.

entries.name: indices_bool_default_oob-errored#5
entries.script: [I1] `Coll[Byte](1,2,3).indices.getOrElse(5, true)`. `indices` is the ONLY in-script route to a specialised `Coll[Int]` (`CollsOverArrays.scala:68` builds it from a concrete `Array[Int]`; no deserializer ever specialises Int), so this is a `$mcI$sp` receiver with a Boolean default: `ClassCastException` to `java.lang.Integer`. **SEPARATING, and the third specialised kind** — the separation is the specialisation itself, on every kind that exists.

entries.name: indices_bool_default_in_range-errored#6
entries.script: [I2] The same at index 0, IN range. **SEPARATING.**

entries.name: int_concrete_bool_default_oob-accept#7
entries.script: [I3] The GENERIC twin, a `ConcreteCollection` of the SAME three ints `(0,1,2)` that `indices` produces: `.getOrElse(5, true)` RETURNS `true` at cost 79. Same declared `Coll[Int]`, same items, same call — and the opposite verdict from I1.

entries.name: int_concrete_bool_default_in_range-accept#8
entries.script: [I4] The same at index 0: returns the element `Int 0` at cost 79, where I2 throws.

entries.name: indices_int_default_oob-accept#9
entries.script: [I5] **CONTROL for I1/I2:** the specialised `indices` receiver with a well-typed Int default returns `9` at cost 75.
